answer: Bind each agent identity to one TPM-backed hardware key: the chip in one physical device signs a fresh challenge tying the agent's key to that device, re-checked every epoch, and a second key claiming the same chip is rejected. Like a reef on one rock, each identity anchors to one piece of hardware — the private key never leaves the TPM, so a software copy cannot sign. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real devices at roughly $35 each, about $35,000, plus enrolling each one by hand. A velvet clone is worthless without the chip, and a garden of fakes withers when it must prove hardware.
